candidates: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) with polyradiculopathy
key_facts: Normal MRI of brain and orbits
Abnormalities in MRI of lumbosacral spine
Nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots
Diffuse heterogeneous signal abnormalities in bone marrow
Cerebrospinal fluid with high white blood cell count
Cerebrospinal fluid with high red blood cell count
champion: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) with polyradiculopathy

raw.champion: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) with polyradiculopathy
raw.rationale: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions, atypical cells/blasts in cerebrospinal fluid, and nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots are highly suggestive of BPDCN with polyradiculopathy, which is a rare and aggressive hematologic malignancy.

rejected.label: Lymphomatous meningitis
rejected.why: While lymphomatous meningitis could explain some of the neurological symptoms, it does not typically cause violaceous cutaneous lesions or the specific pattern of nerve root enhancement seen on MRI.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic polyradiculoneuropathy
rejected.why: Paraneoplastic polyradiculoneuropathy is a condition associated with an underlying cancer, but the presence of atypical cells/blasts in cerebrospinal fluid and specific cutaneous lesions point more directly to a hematologic malignancy like BPDCN.
